chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man fasted while traveling. He said: “If it had reached him that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله prohibited that, then qada is upon him; and if it had not reached him, then there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the state in which the ruling of fasting changes
key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: make-up fasting required after invalid or improper performance
key_terms.بَلَغَهُ: it reached him; he was informed of the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who fasted while traveling without knowing the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had prohibited it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about sawm during travel and ties accountability to whether the person knew of the Prophet’s prohibition. If the ruling had reached him, he must perform qada; if it had not, no liability is upon him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1987 - Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) that he said:

I asked him about a man who fasted while traveling.
The Imam (as) replied: "If he was informed that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited fasting in such a situation, then he must make up for it (qada). However, if he was not aware of this prohibition, then there is no obligation upon him."
